task: AD vs CN, 5-fold subject-level cross-validation over all 501 subjects
verdict: REAL SIGNAL - AUC interval excludes 0.5 by a wide margin

supersedes.note: The previously displayed 82.7% / AUC 0.9055 came from ONE 75-subject test split. Cross-validating the same configuration over all 501 subjects gives 70.9% / 0.7845, and the AUC intervals do not overlap. The single split drew a favourable sample.

threshold_note: Chosen on 501 out-of-fold cross-validation predictions, not on a 75-subject validation split. The previous 0.422 was fitted on 75 subjects and was badly miscalibrated: it called 36% of healthy subjects Alzheimer's (CN recall 63.9% vs AD recall 78.7%) AND scored lower overall (70.3% vs 74.1%). At 0.493 the two classes are treated symmetrically -- CN recall 76.8%, AD recall 70.4%.
